blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence:
export const bucket = (ps: Price[]) =>
  ps.reduce<Record<string, Price[]>>((a, p) => ((a[(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8 ? "hi" : "lo"] ||= []).push(p), a), {});
findings.recommendation: Rewrite `bucket` as a plain function a reader can follow without the plan: a named constant `PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS = 1000` (10 euros, the rule the proposal states), a readable comparison `price.cents >= PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS`, full names (`prices`, `price`, `groups` instead of `ps`, `p`, `a`), and a typed result such as `{ cheap: Price[]; premium: Price[] }` built with two `filter` calls or a simple loop — instead of the `reduce` with a comma expression and `||=` in a computed key. The doc comment speaks of "cheap" and "premium" while the keys are "hi" and "lo", and `Record<string, Price[]>` hides that a key may be missing when no price falls in it; aligning the names and the type removes both questions. Where a newcomer stumbles: the condition `(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8` — nothing says what the shift and the mask mean, nor that 0x3e8 is 1000, and a reader cannot tell whether it is meant to be "10 euros and more". It is not: 512 cents gives 32 & 1000 = 32, so a 5.12-euro price lands in "hi", while 16384 cents gives 1024 & 1000 = 0, so a 163.84-euro price lands in "lo" — the bit mask does not express a threshold at all. The dense shape is what hides this; the developer should confirm the intended rule when rewriting it.
findings.title: `bucket` packs the premium rule into an unreadable bit-twiddling one-liner
